newsitem.title: UK: Britain plans aerial photo mission over Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Britain plans aerial photo mission over Zaire.

text.p: A British photo-reconnaissance plane is expected to fly over eastern Zaire on Friday to assess the refugee crisis, Britain's Ministry of Defence said on Thursday.

A 50-man team and three giant Hercules transport aircraft will accompany the air force Canberra reconnaissance plane which is due to take off from a British base at Akrotiri in Cyprus later on Thursday, a ministry spokesman said.
"A Canberra PR9 should fly to Africa today and begin its operations on Friday," the spokesman told Reuters.
"We're just waiting on a decision on where the plane will land -- where the best place will be to operate from."
The Hercules transports are equipped with mobile photographic cabins enabling the crew to process and enhance photographs in the field.
"The Canberra PR9 uses high-quality optical cameras so you need a support party on the ground to process the film," the spokesman said.
The reconnaissance mission follows Britain's decision to put on hold its plans to send combat troops to eastern Zaire after news that up to 500,000 refugees had returned home to Rwanda.

The government said on Wednesday that Britain remained prepared to take part in a multinational military force in Zaire but alomng with other Western nations needed more information before it could decide how to help refugees returning to Rwanda.
The photo-reconnaissance team is expected to stay in the Great Lakes region for around a week, the ministry said.
